title: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 13](/bible/deuteronomy/13)

**[Deuteronomy 13:5](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v5)</sup> And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee.

- The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High.
- What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.
- Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

  Precepts:
  - **[Romans 16:17](/bible/romans/16#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/romans/16#v17)</sup> Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

    Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them.
  - **[Proverbs 4:2](/bible/proverbs/4#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/proverbs/4#v2)</sup> For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.

    For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law; the doctrine is the law.
  - **[Job 12:16](/bible/job/12#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/job/12#v16)</sup> With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.

    The deceived and the deceiver are his; the judgment is the Most High's, not ours.

**[Deuteronomy 13:6-11](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v6)</sup> If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v7)</sup> Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v8)</sup> Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v9)</sup> But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v10)</sup> And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v11)</sup> And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.

- If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you.
- Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy.
- Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown.
- This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 23:2](/bible/exodus/23#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/23#v2)</sup> Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:

    Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; being enticed to serve other gods is evil, so follow them not.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 4:22](/bible/sirach/4#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/sirach/4#v22)</sup> Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.

    However close or trusted the person, accept no person against thy soul; your salvation is at stake.
  - **[Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1)</sup> And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

    If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; utter what you know instead of concealing it.

**[Deuteronomy 13:12-16](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v12)</sup> If thou shalt hear say in one of thy cities, which the Lord thy God hath given thee to dwell there, saying,
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v13)</sup> Certain men, the children of Belial, are gone out from among you, and have withdrawn the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which ye have not known;
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v14)</sup> Then shalt thou enquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought among you;
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v15)</sup> Thou shalt surely smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein, and the cattle thereof, with the edge of the sword.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v16)</sup> And thou shalt gather all the spoil of it into the midst of the street thereof, and shalt burn with fire the city, and all the spoil thereof every whit, for the Lord thy God: and it shall be an heap for ever; it shall not be built again.

- If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again.
- Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel.
- All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

  Precepts:
  - **[Joshua 7:1](/bible/joshua/7#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/7#v1)</sup> But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.

    Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
  - **[Joshua 7:24-26](/bible/joshua/7#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/joshua/7#v24)</sup> And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/joshua/7#v25)</sup> And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones.
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/joshua/7#v26)</sup> And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day. So the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.

    Joshua and all Israel brought Achan and all he had to the valley of Achor and stoned them with stones; so the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger.
